system.summary: Upside-down writing, applied loosely: German in Latin script with every letter turned top to bottom (b/p, d/q, n/u, m/w trade places; e looks like o, h like y, a like v, i like X, l like j); reflecting a line restores it (Brackx). The prince's own cipher table (sign alphabet and nomenclator 10-70) and a slip nomenclator in the same series are not used by any letter found.
system.sibling_key: Nr. 2 Bd. I image 6 (prince's table) and Nr. 2 Bd. II image 184 (slip key), both unused

prior_solution.where: The 1610 letters were deciphered at the time (interlinear); the Nov 1611 slip has no decipherment. No edition searched for yet.

conditions.human_role: Contributed: Michael Brackx searched the series image by image, identified the system and read the slip's first lines with Claude Code; the project owner set up Claude Code and posed the problem.
tools: Brackx's reflection script (issue #128; not in the repository)

solution.what: Brackx (issue #128): Z 44 A 9a Ic is digitised further than the catalogue row said (Nr. 1 Bd. I-III, Nr. 2 Bd. I-IV, Nr. 3, Nr. 4 Bd. I, Nr. 5, Nr. 6); image URL pattern found.
Brackx described the prince's cipher table (Nr. 2 Bd. I image 6) and a slip nomenclator (Nr. 2 Bd. II image 184); searched about 2,280 images for letters using them; none found.
Brackx identified Alairt's cipher as German written upside down; reflected lines of the 18 May 1610 letter read as German and agree with the interlinear decipherment (date line, opening).

Here: images 6, 241 and 400 fetched; the table is as described; image 241 flipped top to bottom gives Latin-script German with o for e under the dark gloss; slip line 1 transcribed and read as 'Will der Kayser bericht werden, dass der Hertz-', agreeing with Brackx.
Here: the Nov 1611 slip transcribed line by line from per-line crops with the reflected line under the original (texts/slip1611_transcription.txt, 242 letter tokens measured).

Here: slip read by reflection and context: the Emperor is to be told that the Duke of Brunswick leads a disorderly life with loose women, bought a whole house for a public [?] and had [?] built, so that His Majesty has cast his disfavour on him. The writer is not consistent (W for M in Mayt., w kept in werden; t/f/k alike; u/n and e/o swapped). _check_reading: 50 words, hole rate 0.14, 2 of 5 sentences clean. Five words open; by the sentence measure (2 of 5 clean) the slip stays decoded, not read.

outcome.method_basis: The Nov 1611 slip has no decipherment of the time; Brackx identified the system (upside-down German) from the deciphered 1610 letters of the same writer, and the slip was read here by reflection, in part. The 1610 letters carry their own decipherments and are not transcribed yet.
